title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: The flow involves the collection of GPS coordinates, which are considered highly sensitive personal data. The threat exists because the data is collected without explicit, informed consent from the data subject (EE2), and the data type is not functionally required for the basic functionality of the Mobile App Backend.
assumptions: GPS coordinates are classified as sensitive personal data under GDPR.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The flow involves the collection of GPS coordinates at regular intervals. The threat exists because the volume of personal data collected (continuous GPS data) is excessive compared to what is functionally needed for the backend to operate.
assumptions: Regular interval collection implies continuous data flow.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The flow involves the collection of GPS coordinates and their transmission to the backend. The threat exists because the processing of this data is not necessary to achieve the functional goals of the system (e.g., basic app functionality).
assumptions: GPS data is not required for the core functionality of the Mobile App Backend.

title: Involved Parties
description: The flow involves the collection of GPS coordinates and their transmission to the backend. The threat exists because the data is made accessible to the backend (a known, targeted, and scoped party) without additional necessary parties.
assumptions: The backend is a known, targeted, and scoped party.

title: Availability/Accessibility
description: The flow involves the collection of GPS coordinates and their transmission to the backend. The threat exists because the data is published or broadcasted by the system (the backend) to other services or users without additional necessary parties.
assumptions: The backend broadcasts data to other services or users.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: The flow involves the collection of GPS coordinates and their transmission to the backend. The threat exists because the data is implicitly collected as a side-effect of the explicit data flow (transmission).
assumptions: Transmission of data implies collection of the data.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: The mobile app backend writes location data to the Location History Store. Location data is inherently sensitive personal data, and the system collects it without explicit, informed consent or a clear functional necessity for the app's core purpose (e.g., basic navigation). This represents a violation of the data minimization principle, where sensitive data is processed beyond what is strictly required.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The backend processes a continuous stream of location pings. This data is processed more frequently than functionally needed for the app's basic functionality, constituting excessive volume of personal data.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The system processes location data for storage and history, but the processing and treatment of this personal data is not necessary to achieve the functional goals of the app. The data is kept longer than functionally needed.

title: Involved Parties
description: The location history store is a public-facing service. Personal data is made accessible to a broad, predetermined set of external parties (the public) rather than being limited to a targeted and scoped set of users or partners.

title: Availability/Accessibility
description: The location history store is a public-facing service. Personal data is published more broadly than necessary, making it accessible to a wide audience.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: The location history store is a public-facing service. Personal data is implicitly collected as a side-effect of the explicit data flow from the mobile app backend.

assumptions: The data is stored with specific address details beyond what is needed for the basic geofencing logic.

title: Excessive Processing

title: Excessive Exposure
